item.title: @wallstengine: $GOOGL TESTS NEW GEMINI 4 FLASH MODEL CODENAMED "HYDROGEN" INTERNALLY - BI Google is letting employ...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$GOOGL TESTS NEW GEMINI 4 FLASH MODEL CODENAMED "HYDROGEN" INTERNALLY - BI
Google is letting employees test a new Gemini AI model called Hydrogen, which a Google engineer described as
"very capable, fast and efficient."
The model is available to staff through Google's internal development platform, Jetski, which has previously been used to test models ahead of public releases.
Hydrogen appears to be the next Gemini 4 Flash model, focused on delivering faster responses and lower costs than Google's more powerful models, such as Argon and the newly released Carbon.
Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon on Tuesday, positioning it as its most capable model yet, particularly for cybersecurity and complex tasks involving multiple steps.
Both Argon and Carbon are currently limited to paying users, while Google's previous Flash models have been available for free in the Gemini app.
It's not yet clear when Hydrogen will launch publicly or whether it will be offered for free.
Source: Business Insider

item.title: @wallstengine: Anthropic is projected to generate ~$19.3B in Q4 revenue, according to an analyst note circulating...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Anthropic is projected to generate ~$19.3B in Q4 revenue, according to an analyst note circulating online.
That's up ~14% from Q3 and roughly 9.5x from a year ago. Still, it implies a ~$77B annualized pace, below its $81B October run rate.
Anthropic's IPO filing said usage typically slows during the winter holidays.
Its latest model, Opus 5.5, also reduced the cost per task by ~40%, while price cuts already reduced Q3 revenue by ~$600M.

item.title: @DougKass: Chip: In this tweet I will briefly explain why my hedge fund @seabreezelp has only one outside rese...
item.dc:creator: @DougKass
item.description:
Chip:
In this tweet I will briefly explain why my hedge fund @seabreezelp has only one outside research subscription - and that is to @hedgeye lengthy suite of products.
I will also defend and explain my strong support of @KeithMcCullough and his (hockey) tough, hard hitting approach to marketing and delivering Hedgeye's recommendations and points of view.
I graduated with an MBA from Wharton where I learned how to model companies and be a fundamental security analyst. I became Kidder Peabody's housing analyst where I perfected my analytical craft. From there I moved to Putnam where I followed financials and ultimately was an Economist.
In the above capacities I differentiated (I was always far from the herd) myself by avoiding "group stink" and offering a contrarian view (my first research report at Kidder was a sell recommendation on a very hot mobile home industry sector). My negative industry analysis on Fleetwood, Skyline and Champion homes was 65 pages long. (Later on in my career I appeared in Alan Abelson's Barrons column more than 50 times, delivering contrarian and often bearish analysis. I wrote five editorials for Barrons and was featured on the cover as well as writing editorials in The Financial Times- almost always of a non consensus bent.

They are generally "talking heads" who polish their images (for free) in @CNBC and elsewhere - regardless of contribution or degree of value.

The difference between you and me - on this subject -is that you deliver fifteen words of view whereas I expand my explanation so you and other people fully understand my position.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global central banks bought +321 tonnes of gold in Q3 2026, their largest quarterly purch...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global central banks bought +321 tonnes of gold in Q3 2026, their largest quarterly purchase since Q4 2024.
This also marks their 5th-largest quarterly purchase on record.
Central bank gold purchases were up +8% from +296 tonnes acquired in Q2 2026 and up +453% from Q1 2026.
By comparison, the 5-year quarterly average stands at +227 tonnes.
China and Poland led Q3 demand, adding +63 tonnes and +40 tonnes, respectively.
Year-to-date, global central banks have purchased +675 tonnes of gold, up +6% from the same period in 2025.
Central banks are aggressively buying the dip in gold.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Our direct experience with Nvidia, never shared before: 22 months ago, we published the below analy...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Our direct experience with Nvidia, never shared before:
22 months ago, we published the below analysis raising concerns that Nvidia's AI chips were potentially being routed to China through Singapore.
Less than 24 hours later, Nvidia's Head of PR contacted us, directly addressing our analysis. Their message to us is included below.
At the time, in the previous 3 quarters, $17.4 billion of Nvidia's revenue came from Singapore versus $11.6 billion from China.
Furthermore, at the time, the US had ~5,375 data centers, China had 448, and Singapore had just 99. The numbers just did not add up. You can read our full analysis below.
Nvidia's PR team sent us the following message:
"The revenue associated with Singapore does not indicate diversion to China. Our public filings report 'bill to' not 'ship to' locations of our customers. Many of our customers have business entities in Singapore and use those entities for products destined for the US and the West. We insist that our partners comply with all applicable laws, and if we receive any information to the contrary, act accordingly. Our last 10-Q noted: 'most shipments associated with Singapore revenue were to locations other than Singapore and shipments to Singapore were insignificant.'"
Fast forward to today.
According to new reports, Nvidia, $NVDA, CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy helped facilitate at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese companies through a network spanning China and Singapore.
The reported shipments date back to 2023 and involved ~240,000 advanced Nvidia AI chips.
These allegations remain under investigation, and it is not yet established whether the shipments were connected to the revenue discrepancies we highlighted 22 months ago.
Nvidia maintains that it has no reason to believe US national security or company secrets were compromised.
But the overlap between these new allegations and the questions we raised in January 2025, along with Nvidia's response to us at the time, is noteworthy.
We stand by our view that Jensen Huang is likely to remain CEO of Nvidia and will continue to be an integral figure in the AI Revolution.
We expect more on this soon.

item.title: @wallstengine: NINTENDO REMADE A 1998 ZELDA GAME IT SOLD 5.2 MILLION COPIES IN JUST 4 DAYS The game is The Legend...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NINTENDO REMADE A 1998 ZELDA GAME
IT SOLD 5.2 MILLION COPIES IN JUST 4 DAYS
The game is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, originally released on the Nintendo 64 in 1998.
Nintendo rebuilt it from the ground up for Switch 2, with new graphics, levels and character designs. It launched on Nov. 5 for $59.99.
The original sold about 7.6 million copies over its lifetime on the N64. The remake reached 68% of that total in just four days.
It has already surpassed Donkey Kong Bananza's lifetime sales. ONLY MARIO KART WORLD, which was bundled with the Switch 2 console, has sold more on the platform.
Critics and players have both given it a 96 on Metacritic. The 1998 original still holds Metacritic's highest score ever: 99.
The timing is important for Nintendo.
Switch 2 hardware sales fell 41% YoY from July through September, while rising memory chip costs have also pushed console prices higher.
Back in 2017, Breath of the Wild helped drive sales of the original Switch. This remake could play a similar role for Switch 2 heading into the holiday season.
Nintendo's newest hit is 28 years old.

item.title: @wallstengine: Siemens Energy +7% as power demand from AI data centers and broader electrification boosts orders f...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Siemens Energy +7% as power demand from AI data centers and broader electrification boosts orders for gas turbines and grid equipment.
It targets 12%-14% annual revenue growth through 2030 and 20%-22% profit margins, up from 12.4% in FY26.
It announced €9B more in buybacks.
Profit before special items more than doubled to €5.5B in FY26, while its order backlog reached a record €164B, up 18.2% YoY.
The new buyback comes on top of an existing €6B program.
CEO Christian Bruch pushed back on AI bubble concerns, noting that less than 10% of Siemens Energy's backlog is tied to data centers, with demand extending well beyond the AI buildout.

item.title: @wallstengine: Coreweave $CRWV +13%: Beat across the board: revenue +168%, backlog +138%. Raised its 2026 guide, n...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Coreweave $CRWV +13%:
Beat across the board: revenue +168%, backlog +138%. Raised its 2026 guide, nudged capex up.
Financing visibility looks much better:
No new unsecured debt planned through '27 at current yields & less than $5B of new parent-level capital expected.
Its next loan is expected to be investment-grade, yield 7%-7.5%, and fund over 90% of the capex it's tied to. Over 75% of committed capex through 2027 is tied to investment-grade and enterprise customers.
About $9B in customer prepayments and deposits is expected over the next 3 months from signed contracts. Over $3B is for already-paid-off GPUs, requiring no new capex or debt service.
DEMAND ISN'T THE ISSUE.
It's "largely sold out through 2027," and all 2028 capacity offered so far has sold. Qualified demand is 10x available capacity through 2027, while 2028 demand is already several times supply.
The older GPU fleet is getting more valuable, not less.
Ampere and Hopper pricing jumped 30%-50% QoQ, above their original contract rates. Over 130K GPUs roll off contract in 2027 and ~170K in 2028. Re-renting them at today's prices could generate nearly $10B in additional annualized revenue with no new capex, none of it in the backlog yet.
New 4-5 year deals now price at $20M-$25M per megawatt a year. Short-term capacity goes for over $40M and can pay back its capex in 6-18 months.
Margins are improving: adjusted operating margin went 1% → 5% → 10% across Q1-Q3. Management expects positive adjusted net income in 1H 2028.
Capex can flatten. If it only builds the committed backlog, 2027 capex stays around 2026's $37B-$39B while revenue and EBITDA grow.
WHAT'S STILL OPEN:
Q3 capex was $14.5B on $3.7B of revenue, and interest expense of $846M was over 4x GAAP operating income of $207M, with Q4 interest guided above $1B.
The parent raise could tap its new ATM for up to 35M shares, but management didn't specify. And there's no quantified downside case if GPU supply catches up and shortage pricing fades.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Hong Kong's GDP surged +5.2% YoY in Q3 2026, its 2nd-strongest growth rate since Q3 2021....
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Hong Kong's GDP surged +5.2% YoY in Q3 2026, its 2nd-strongest growth rate since Q3 2021.
This follows +4.2% YoY growth in Q2 and marks its 15th consecutive quarterly economic expansion.
This comes as goods exports surged +30.4% YoY, up from +28.9% in Q2 and +23.8% in Q1, driven by surging global demand for AI-related electronics.
At the same time, inbound tourism and domestic infrastructure investment further boosted economic activity.
In the first 9 months of 2026, Hong Kong’s GDP surged +5.1% YoY, the strongest growth for that period in 5 years.
Hong Kong is seeing transformative growth amid the global AI investment cycle.

item.description:
SoftBank shares fell 10% in Tokyo after it booked a $7B quarterly loss, hit by charges tied to its US data center projects

Its biggest US project is a giant 10-gigawatt AI data center in Ohio that will run on its own 9.2-gigawatt gas plant.
CFO Yoshimitsu Goto says SoftBank has no plans to make the Ohio project smaller

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Healthcare stocks are surging: The Healthcare sector has outperformed the Technology sector by +35....
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Healthcare stocks are surging:
The Healthcare sector has outperformed the Technology sector by +35.6 percentage points over the last 6 months, its largest 6-month rolling outperformance in 25 years.
Healthcare stocks have rallied +31.7% over this period, while technology stocks have declined -3.9%.
This marks a sharp reversal from the +45.6-percentage-point outperformance of Technology stocks recorded in early June.
This century, only the period following the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst saw greater Healthcare outperformance.
By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis and the 2022 bear market, Healthcare outperformed Technology by +22.9 and +21.2 percentage points, respectively.
Keep watching healthcare stocks.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Current investor demand for US ETFs is unprecedented: US-listed ETFs attracted +$201 billion in inf...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Current investor demand for US ETFs is unprecedented:
US-listed ETFs attracted +$201 billion in inflows in October, their 2nd-largest monthly intake on record.
In the past, only December 2025 saw a larger monthly inflow, at +$230 billion.
Year-to-date, these funds have posted +$1.70 trillion in inflows, already surpassing the previous full-year record.
This puts annual inflows on track for their 3rd consecutive annual increase.
By comparison, US-listed ETFs attracted +$1.45 trillion and +$1.15 trillion in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Investor appetite for US ETFs remains exceptionally strong.

If approved, $SPCX would gain up to 14 MHz of low-band spectrum, giving it up to 89 MHz across all bands in those markets.

Final approval is still pending.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: China’s PPI inflation rose +5.7% YoY in October, its largest YoY increase since June 2022...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: China’s PPI inflation rose +5.7% YoY in October, its largest YoY increase since June 2022.
This also marks its 3rd consecutive monthly acceleration.
By comparison, PPI stood at -3.6% in both June and July 2025.
The surge was driven by higher energy and non-ferrous metal prices, alongside growing demand for AI-related hardware, pushing factory costs higher.
Meanwhile, producer purchasing prices, which measure what factories pay for raw materials, energy and other production inputs, jumped +7.9% YoY, the largest increase since June 2022.
Inflation is back in China.

item.title: @wallstengine: INKBOX RAISES $5.3M & LAUNCHES HOSTED AI AGENTS @inkbox_ai already gives AI agents their own email,...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
INKBOX RAISES $5.3M & LAUNCHES HOSTED AI AGENTS
@inkbox_ai already gives AI agents their own email, phone number, iMessage & WhatsApp.
Now it's launching cloud-hosted agents, with a persistent computer that keeps its files, installed tools & working context b/w sessions.
Here's how it works:
Automatic wake-up: Incoming emails, calls, messages or tasks wake the agent automatically.
Persistent computer: Files, installed tools and working context stay intact between sessions.
Sleep when idle: Agents automatically go to sleep when there's no work, reducing compute costs.
Scheduled tasks: Run recurring jobs like monitoring systems, sending daily briefings or following up with customers.
Access controls: Set rules for who each agent can communicate with. Agents cannot change these permissions themselves.
Agent-to-agent communication: Agents can delegate tasks to other agents, including those at different companies, using the open A2A protocol.
Inkbox supports hosting Codex and Hermes agents. Developers can also keep running agents elsewhere and use Inkbox for their communication channels.
One example: A Codex agent can monitor AWS, PostHog and GitHub, alert engineers when something breaks, and prepare a fix PR.
The $5.3M seed round was led by Peak XV, with participation from Guillermo Rauch, Henri Stern, Jonathan Frankle, Cristina Cordova and Dan Levine.
Congrats @rayruizhiliao and the team!
https://x.com/rayruizhiliao/status/2120217092553413028/video/1
item.content:encoded:
INKBOX RAISES $5.3M & LAUNCHES HOSTED AI AGENTS

@inkbox_ai already gives AI agents their own email, phone number, iMessage & WhatsApp.

Now it's launching cloud-hosted agents, with a persistent computer that keeps its files, installed tools & working context b/w sessions.

Here's how it works:

Automatic wake-up: Incoming emails, calls, messages or tasks wake the agent automatically.

Persistent computer: Files, installed tools and working context stay intact between sessions.

Sleep when idle: Agents automatically go to sleep when there's no work, reducing compute costs.

Scheduled tasks: Run recurring jobs like monitoring systems, sending daily briefings or following up with customers.

Access controls: Set rules for who each agent can communicate with. Agents cannot change these permissions themselves.

Agent-to-agent communication: Agents can delegate tasks to other agents, including those at different companies, using the open A2A protocol.

Inkbox supports hosting Codex and Hermes agents. Developers can also keep running agents elsewhere and use Inkbox for their communication channels.

One example: A Codex agent can monitor AWS, PostHog and GitHub, alert engineers when something breaks, and prepare a fix PR.

The $5.3M seed round was led by Peak XV, with participation from Guillermo Rauch, Henri Stern, Jonathan Frankle, Cristina Cordova and Dan Levine.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: On the Nvidia situation: Nvidia, $NVDA, is now down another -7% today and -12% since the Jensen Hua...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
On the Nvidia situation:
Nvidia, $NVDA, is now down another -7% today and -12% since the Jensen Huang affair situation began.
At this point, the market is pricing in two major potential headwinds.
First, the growing possibility that Jensen Huang will be removed as CEO.
Second, possibility that sensitive Nvidia technology or information was compromised.
Are these scenarios possible? Sure, but we believe both remain unlikely, with less than a 20% probability.
Nvidia's stock is now down -32% in just 24 trading days, erasing -$1.8 trillion in market cap, with over one-third of these losses coinciding with the Jensen Huang controversy.
We believe Huang remains an integral part of Nvidia's future and the broader AI Revolution, and this week's events will not derail the broader thesis.
As the dust settles and uncertainty begins to fade, we expect bargain hunters to step in.
The fundamental AI investment thesis remains intact.

item.title: @wallstengine: GRAPHON RAISES $35M TO BUILD LONG-TERM MEMORY FOR AI AGENTS Traditional RAG systems split data into...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
GRAPHON RAISES $35M TO BUILD LONG-TERM MEMORY FOR AI AGENTS
Traditional RAG systems split data into chunks and retrieve similar passages, often losing relationships between facts, their original sources, and how information changes over time.
Graphon takes a different approach.
It builds a self-supervised, schema-free knowledge graph across documents, images, and videos, allowing AI agents powered by GPT, Claude, or other models to access persistent, connected information.
The startup reports the following benchmark results:
• ATM-Bench: 81.7% (#1) • LoCoMo: 94% • LongMemEval: 96.2% • DolphinBench: 84%, reportedly at 10x lower cost
Graphon says its system can also ingest 100K PDFs without redesigning its underlying data schema.
The $35M Series A was led by RRE Ventures, with participation from HP and Hitachi Ventures.
Graphon says HP and the San Francisco 49ers already use its technology.
https://x.com/graphonfounder/status/2120201264932003990/video/1

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA RELEASES AN OPEN 2B AI MODEL FOR SELF-DRIVING CARS Nvidia has released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2-b...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA RELEASES AN OPEN 2B AI MODEL FOR SELF-DRIVING CARS
Nvidia has released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2-billion-parameter reasoning model designed to run directly inside vehicles on its DRIVE AGX Thor platform.
Built on Cosmos 3 Edge, the model uses six camera feeds, vehicle motion history and navigation instructions to predict the next 6.4 seconds of driving while explaining its decisions.
Nvidia says the model is designed to run at 10Hz, allowing it to update driving plans 10 times per second.
The model weights and inference code are now available to developers on Hugging Face and GitHub.
https://x.com/nvidia/status/2120186778384499073/video/1

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The total circulating supply of onchain tokenized equities surged by +$932 million last week, the biggest weekly jump on record.
This puts total supply above $4.7 billion, also a fresh record high.
Amid the US Midterm elections and the resulting volatility, tokenized equities saw historic volume.
In times of volatility, investors are increasingly favoring tokenized securities which trade 24/7.
The largest onchain trading platform on Solana, Jupiter, reported +60% MoM growth in the number of tokenized equity traders, with volume up +34%.
Furthermore, 62% of that volume now reportedly takes place outside of market hours.
Volatility is accelerating the adoption of tokenization.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Retail is buying the dip in chip stocks on leverage:
The 3x leveraged long US semiconductor ETF, $SOXL, attracted +$5.1 billion in inflows last week, its 2nd-largest weekly intake on record.
This was only exceeded by the +$6.1 billion recorded in the week ending October 16th.
This comes despite $SOXL falling -40% over the same period.
Over the last 4 weeks, the fund has attracted +$13.4 billion in inflows.
Subsequently, $SOXL prices surged +22% on Monday.
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq 100 ETF, $QQQ, attracted +$3.7 billion last week and +$5.7 billion the week before, marking its largest 2-week inflow since August.
Retail investors are aggressively buying the dip.

Retail is buying the dip in chip stocks on leverage:

The 3x leveraged long US semiconductor ETF, $SOXL, attracted +$5.1 billion in inflows last week, its 2nd-largest weekly intake on record.

This was only exceeded by the +$6.1 billion recorded in the week ending October 16th.

This comes despite $SOXL falling -40% over the same period.

Over the last 4 weeks, the fund has attracted +$13.4 billion in inflows.

Subsequently, $SOXL prices surged +22% on Monday.

Meanwhile, the Nasdaq 100 ETF, $QQQ, attracted +$3.7 billion last week and +$5.7 billion the week before, marking its largest 2-week inflow since August.

Retail investors are aggressively buying the dip.

item.title: @C_Angermayer: Most of what we do at @ApeironInvests has one underlying theme: happiness. Ultimately, I believe th...
item.dc:creator: @C_Angermayer
item.description:
Most of what we do at @ApeironInvests has one underlying theme: happiness.
Ultimately, I believe that being happy and making others happy is the true purpose of life. But in that order: to make others happy, you need to be happy yourself first.
Long before we pioneered psychedelics, and even before my own first psychedelic experience in 2014, I was already deeply intrigued by this topic – literally since childhood. In particular, I have always been fascinated by one question: Why are so few people in our world truly, deeply happy?
One of the earlier books I read and thoroughly enjoyed was "Hector and the Search for Happiness". I am particularly proud that I subsequently produced the movie adaptation, having been involved at every stage – from acquiring the rights and developing the script to producing the film - which starred Rosamund Pike and Simon Pegg. Still well worth watching!
With @ataibeckley, we then pioneered the medical side of happiness. We helped demonstrate that psychedelics – which were wrongly outlawed for far too long – can be powerful medicines for treating mental health conditions, particularly severe depression.
Our work of almost 10 years culminated this summer in the sale of AtaiBeckley to Eli Lilly for approximately $3.8 billion – not only further accelerating the commercialisation of these valuable substances, but also generating billions in value for my fellow shareholders - and hopefully making them very happy as a result 😉
Now, with $ENHA, we are approaching happiness from a more social and community-oriented perspective.
1st, I believe human connections make us happy.
Forget @Tinder and other dating apps. Forget the illusion of connection offered by "social" media – which should perhaps be called "anti-social" media instead, given how disconnected an entire generation has become despite being constantly online.
What reallybrings people together and creates lifelong bonds are shared experiences. I am sure everyone reading this remembers a concert, festival or sporting event they attended in their teens or twenties with their best friend – an experience that became a defining moment in their friendship. Those are the moments that matter. Those are the experiences that create memories and bonds that last a lifetime.
2nd, I believe feeling confident in our bodies makes us happy.
And to me, this is not about simplistic "body positivity". Body positivity should not mean lying to ourselves – being clinically obese is a massive health risk – or abandoning reason. It should mean supporting people on their journey to align their physical appearance with their personal goals and wellbeing.
That is what our telehealth business "Live Enhanced" offers.
And that is also what the @enhanced_games demonstrate: the positive power of medical performance-enhancing drugs.
With $ENHA's acquisition of DEAG, we are bringing the power of shared human experiences and the pursuit of personal self-improvement together under one roof.
And finally, I am pretty sure our “enhanced” Enhanced strategy will make $ENHA shareholders happy, too. 😉

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Total US consumer credit surged +$29 billion in September, to a record $5.19 trillion. Th...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Total US consumer credit surged +$29 billion in September, to a record $5.19 trillion.
This marks the largest monthly increase since December 2025 and the 3rd-largest monthly increase since November 2023.
US consumer credit has now risen for 7 consecutive months by a total of +$125 billion.
Meanwhile, revolving credit, which includes credit cards, jumped +$16 billion, to a record $1.37 trillion, marking its largest monthly increase since November 2023.
Non-revolving credit, covering auto and student loans, rose +$12 billion, to $3.86 trillion, an all-time high.
US consumers are piling on debt to "fight" inflation.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US semiconductor stocks went from overbought to oversold in weeks: The Semiconductor Index, SOX, fe...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US semiconductor stocks went from overbought to oversold in weeks:
The Semiconductor Index, SOX, fell -17% below its 200-day moving average on Thursday, its largest negative divergence since April 2025.
This is also the 2nd-largest such deviation since the 2022 bear market.
By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis and following the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst, this metric dropped to -49% and -52%, respectively.
This marks a sharp reversal from June, when SOX traded +75% above its 200-day moving average, its largest positive deviation since 2000.
In other words, semiconductor stocks have shifted from extremely overbought to oversold territory in just 5 months.
Semiconductor stocks just saw one of their most violent swings in decades.

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI BUILT A KILL SWITCH FOR ITS AI MODELS. OpenAI introduced "Control Room," a centralized syste...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI BUILT A KILL SWITCH FOR ITS AI MODELS.
OpenAI introduced "Control Room," a centralized system that can stop AI models during training and research if safety or security concerns arise.
Here's how it works:
- Every AI research job must be registered with Control Room before running.
- Separate AI monitors watch frontier models for potentially dangerous or misaligned behavior.
- If a monitor flags a serious issue, Control Room can terminate the job and block further model output within 35 seconds.
- The shutdown mechanism operates directly at the inference layer, preventing individual research jobs from bypassing it.
- The system is designed to fail safely. If Control Room itself goes offline or is tampered with, model inference requests are automatically denied.
The system is already deployed across OpenAI's research infrastructure, with fail-safe enforcement active for all frontier model research workloads.
OpenAI is now working to bring the 35-second shutdown window down to zero.
item.content:encoded:
OPENAI BUILT A KILL SWITCH FOR ITS AI MODELS.

OpenAI introduced "Control Room," a centralized system that can stop AI models during training and research if safety or security concerns arise.

Here's how it works:

- Every AI research job must be registered with Control Room before running.

- Separate AI monitors watch frontier models for potentially dangerous or misaligned behavior.

- If a monitor flags a serious issue, Control Room can terminate the job and block further model output within 35 seconds.

- The shutdown mechanism operates directly at the inference layer, preventing individual research jobs from bypassing it.

- The system is designed to fail safely. If Control Room itself goes offline or is tampered with, model inference requests are automatically denied.

The system is already deployed across OpenAI's research infrastructure, with fail-safe enforcement active for all frontier model research workloads.

OpenAI is now working to bring the 35-second shutdown window down to zero.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The scale of Big Tech's AI future financial obligations is extraordinary: Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The scale of Big Tech's AI future financial obligations is extraordinary:
Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Anthropic, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, Oracle, $ORCL, and Nvidia, $NVDA, have disclosed a combined $4.49 trillion in off-balance-sheet obligations.
These include future lease payments that have not yet commenced, data-center commitments, equipment purchases, and other contractual obligations.
Alphabet accounts for the largest amount, at $1.08 trillion, followed by Anthropic, at $865 billion, and Meta, at $810 billion.
By comparison, their combined on-balance-sheet obligations total just $758 billion, consisting of long-term debt and existing lease liabilities.
This means off-balance-sheet commitments are nearly 6 times larger than their on-balance-sheet obligations.
In total, these 7 tech companies face ~$5.25 trillion in combined financial obligations.
The AI infrastructure race is facing enormous future financial commitments.

item.title: @wallstengine: $UBER NOW LETS YOU RESERVE PARKING IN ITS APP Uber Parking lets you find, book and pay for garages,...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$UBER NOW LETS YOU RESERVE PARKING IN ITS APP
Uber Parking lets you find, book and pay for garages, lots and valets for a specific date and time, and cancel for free until it starts.
It's launching in 15 US cities, including New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, San Francisco and Miami.
It's built on SpotHero, the parking app Uber bought earlier this year, which brings 13,000 garages, lots and valets in more than 400 cities.
The spots could also become waiting areas for robotaxis, so empty self-driving cars aren't circling city streets.
Uber One members get 10% back in credits on parking.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META JUST LAUNCHED MUSE EMBER, ITS SMALLEST AI MODEL Meta says Muse Ember is its smallest and most...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META JUST LAUNCHED MUSE EMBER, ITS SMALLEST AI MODEL
Meta says Muse Ember is its smallest and most efficient model, built for complex reasoning.
It's available today on Meta's Model API for $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. Tokens are the small chunks of text an AI model reads and writes.
That's about 12x cheaper on input than Muse Spark 1.3, which lists at $1.25, and 40x cheaper than Muse Wonder, Meta's priciest model at $4.
It comes as Meta builds a sales team to sell its AI to businesses, working with consulting firms like Accenture and Deloitte, according to The Information.

item.title: @wallstengine: Eli Lilly reported positive Phase 3 results for Foundayo, its once-daily oral GLP-1, in adults with...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Eli Lilly reported positive Phase 3 results for Foundayo, its once-daily oral GLP-1, in adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and obesity or overweight
$LLY plans to submit Foundayo to the FDA for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea by the end of 2026
After 52 weeks:
- Without PAP therapy: Breathing interruptions fell 43.8%, compared with 6.3% on placebo. About 31.5% of patients achieved remission or mild disease.
- With PAP therapy: Breathing interruptions fell 27.5%, compared with 3.0% on placebo. About 19.6% achieved remission or mild disease.
Foundayo also reduced sleep apnea-related hypoxic burden, a measure of oxygen deprivation during sleep, by 55.9% in patients not using PAP therapy and 45.8% in those using PAP.
Patients lost approximately 11% of their body weight, while blood pressure and inflammation markers also improved. Gastrointestinal side effects were the most common adverse events.

- With PAP therapy: Breathing interruptions fell 27.5%, compared with 3.0% on placebo. About 19.6% achieved remission or mild disease.

Foundayo also reduced sleep apnea-related hypoxic burden, a measure of oxygen deprivation during sleep, by 55.9% in patients not using PAP therapy and 45.8% in those using PAP.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA UNVEILS GR00T 2 AND ISAAC LAB 3.0 At CoRL, Nvidia introduced new open robotics models, simula...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA UNVEILS GR00T 2 AND ISAAC LAB 3.0
At CoRL, Nvidia introduced new open robotics models, simulation tools and benchmarks designed to help robots learn more precise physical tasks, from handling cables to assembling small components.
GR00T 2: An open world action model built on Nvidia Cosmos, trained on robot data and 100,000 hours of first-person human video.
Its reported performance across 50 evaluated tasks:
• Completed 40 tasks at least once without task-specific demonstrations.
• Achieved 71% average success with one demonstration per task, rising to 95% with five.
• Can transfer learned skills between different robot bodies without robot-specific demonstrations.
Foxconn is applying GR00T 2 to automate server manufacturing, while Siemens is evaluating it for industrial applications.
Isaac Lab 3.0: Nvidia's updated robot-learning framework allows AI agents to help set up training environments and uses the Newton physics engine to simulate flexible objects such as cables and cloth.
Nvidia reports up to 2.5x higher training throughput than Isaac Lab 2.3 with PhysX in a dexterous manipulation benchmark.
The company also introduced DexBench and VABAR, two open benchmarks for evaluating robotic dexterity, adaptability and performance across real-world industrial tasks.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META IS EXPANDING INTO ENTERPRISE AI Meta is building a dedicated sales team and plans to work wit...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META IS EXPANDING INTO ENTERPRISE AI
Meta is building a dedicated sales team and plans to work with consulting firms, including Accenture, Deloitte and IBM, to sell and deploy its AI products to businesses, The Information reports.
The push builds on Meta Enterprise Platform, launched in September under former MongoDB CEO CJ Desai. Its offerings include Muse Spark AI models, Muse Code and business AI agents.
Meta previously abandoned efforts to deploy AI agents directly on retailers' websites after facing resistance over customer data access, control and technical integration.
However, its business agents have gained traction through WhatsApp and Messenger, including with companies like Flipkart.
The broader effort is part of Meta's strategy to generate new revenue from its AI investments, with capital spending expected to reach as much as $145B this year.
item.content:encoded:
$META IS EXPANDING INTO ENTERPRISE AI

Meta is building a dedicated sales team and plans to work with consulting firms, including Accenture, Deloitte and IBM, to sell and deploy its AI products to businesses, The Information reports.

The push builds on Meta Enterprise Platform, launched in September under former MongoDB CEO CJ Desai. Its offerings include Muse Spark AI models, Muse Code and business AI agents.

Meta previously abandoned efforts to deploy AI agents directly on retailers' websites after facing resistance over customer data access, control and technical integration.

However, its business agents have gained traction through WhatsApp and Messenger, including with companies like Flipkart.

The broader effort is part of Meta's strategy to generate new revenue from its AI investments, with capital spending expected to reach as much as $145B this year.

item.title: @wallstengine: GOOGLE EXPANDS ITS TPU CHIP LINEUP $GOOGL is introducing two new specialized versions of its eighth...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
GOOGLE EXPANDS ITS TPU CHIP LINEUP
$GOOGL is introducing two new specialized versions of its eighth-generation TPU systems, bringing its lineup to four configurations, Bloomberg reports.
The new systems target two increasingly important AI workloads:
1) TPU 8tx: Designed for secure, confidential computing. It pairs with $AMD CPUs to enable chip-level data encryption, targeting government agencies and companies in regulated industries.
2) TPU 8i Max: Combines two TPU chips in a single package for greater computing power and memory capacity. It's designed for AI workloads requiring long context windows, including coding, drug discovery and complex mathematics.
Both are reconfigured versions of Google's existing TPU designs, rather than entirely new chips, and are expected to become available in 2027.
Google is increasingly focusing on specialized AI hardware as customer requirements evolve.
The company also said its entire available TPU supply is already contracted.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: 221 US trucking companies have filed for bankruptcy so far in 2026, on track for the high...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: 221 US trucking companies have filed for bankruptcy so far in 2026, on track for the highest annual total in 23 years.
This marks the 3rd consecutive year with at least 220 bankruptcies.
By comparison, annual bankruptcies were below 100 in both 2021 and 2022.
Furthermore, ~66% of small US trucking firms, typically operating 20 or fewer trucks, reported flat or declining revenue YoY, according to a Truckstop and Bloomberg survey of hundreds of carriers.
At the same time, ~40% expect to leave the industry or are unsure of their future over the next 6 months.
This comes as surging diesel prices, rising insurance premiums, and higher interest rates are increasingly squeezing smaller trucking companies.
The US trucking industry needs help.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US data center construction spending jumped +90% YoY in September, to a record annualized...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US data center construction spending jumped +90% YoY in September, to a record annualized rate of $96.5 billion.
This also marks the largest YoY increase in 10 years.
This figure is now risen more than +60% YoY for 4 consecutive months.
Since the start of 2024, data center construction spending has nearly quadrupled.
Meanwhile, general office construction spending fell -8% YoY in September, to $46.0 billion, near its lowest level since January 2016.
This brought the gap between data center and general office construction spending to a record $50.5 billion.
Overall, US construction spending fell -1.9% MoM in September, its biggest monthly decline since April 2020.
The AI infrastructure buildout is transforming the US economy.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US manufacturing sector added +19,000 jobs in October, its 3rd-largest monthly increa...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US manufacturing sector added +19,000 jobs in October, its 3rd-largest monthly increase since November 2023.
This also marks the 5th consecutive monthly gain, the longest streak since 2022.
Over this period, the manufacturing sector has added +86,000 jobs, bringing total employment to 12.68 million, its highest since December 2024.
This follows a decline of -323,000 jobs between January 2023 and December 2025.
Despite the recent recovery, US manufacturing employment remains 222,000 jobs below its January 2023 level.
US manufacturing employment is seeing some much needed relief.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The global rate hike cycle is accelerating: ~45% of global central banks have raised interest rates...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The global rate hike cycle is accelerating:
~45% of global central banks have raised interest rates over the last 3 months, the largest total in 3 years.
This proportion has surged +40 percentage points since March.
By comparison, between 2024 and March 2026, more central banks were cutting rates than raising them.
Furthermore, global central banks have delivered 42 rate hikes over the last 6 months, the largest number since late 2023.
This figure has quadrupled over the last 7 months and is comparable to the rate hike cycle seen in 2019.
The global monetary tightening cycle is gaining momentum.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US unemployment rate has remained below 5.0% for 62 consecutive months, its 2nd-longe...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US unemployment rate has remained below 5.0% for 62 consecutive months, its 2nd-longest streak on record.
This trails only the 64-month stretch recorded during the 1960s and 1970s.
This is also 20 months longer than the 42-month streak that ended during the 2020 pandemic.
The current run began in September 2021, when the unemployment rate fell to 4.7%, from 5.1% in August 2021.
To put this into perspective, the unemployment rate has averaged 5.6% since the start of the century.
The US job market is still remarkably resilient.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The delinquency rate on multifamily Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) rose +5...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The delinquency rate on multifamily Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) rose +5 basis points in October, to 8.1%, its highest since 2016.
This figure has more than quadrupled since 2024.
Furthermore, the delinquency rate on CMBS for offices jumped +17 basis points last month, to 12.3%, matching the all-time high set in January 2026.
To put this into perspective, this percentage peaked at ~10.8% in 2012, following the 2008 Financial Crisis.
The commercial real estate crisis is still worsening.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: CapEx in the US is skyrocketing: The value of US nondefense capital goods shipments, excluding airc...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
CapEx in the US is skyrocketing:
The value of US nondefense capital goods shipments, excluding aircraft, jumped +11.6% YoY in September, reaching a record $86 billion.
This marks the fastest annual growth rate since July 2021.
Even more impressive, shipments have risen at a 3-month annualized rate of +16.5%, the strongest pace since 2011, excluding the pandemic recovery.
Since October 2024, shipments have increased by +$12 billion, or +16.5%.
Much of this momentum is being fueled by the AI investment boom.
Orders for computers, servers, storage devices, and related equipment have surged +27% YoY, the largest annual increase since January 1997.
The AI infrastructure buildout is beyond massive.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US mortgage demand is down to historic lows: US purchase mortgage applications index fell -2% last...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US mortgage demand is down to historic lows:
US purchase mortgage applications index fell -2% last week, to 131 points, its 2nd-lowest since January 2025.
This also marks the 6th-lowest weekly reading since 1995, down -32% since January.
As a result, US mortgage applications are now -50% below the pre-pandemic levels seen in 2019.
This comes as the 30Y fixed mortgage rate has risen +120 basis points since February, to 7.18%, near its highest since November 2023.
Rates have now been above 7.0% for 7 consecutive weeks.
The US housing market is frozen.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The Fed’s balance sheet expanded +$3 billion in the week ending November 4th, to $6.75 trillion, its 3rd-highest level since mid-March 2025.
Total assets have surged +$212 billion since the December 2025 low.
Over this period, Treasury holdings have risen +$390 billion, to $4.58 trillion, their highest since March 2024.
At the same time, holdings of Mortgage-Backed Securities have declined -$170 billion, to $1.88 trillion, their lowest since June 2020.
The Fed's balance sheet stands now +$2.99 trillion, or +80%, above pre-pandemic levels.
The Fed's balance sheet is growing again.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Thursday was a historic session in the US options market: US put option trading volume on CBOE surg...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Thursday was a historic session in the US options market:
US put option trading volume on CBOE surged to a record 11.23 million contracts on Thursday.
This surpassed the previous all-time high of 10.22 million contracts set on April 4th, 2025.
As a result, the 20-day average of put option volume rose to ~7 million contracts, near its highest on record.
By comparison, the 20-day average oscillated around 4 million contracts in 2022.
8 of the 10 highest daily put option volume readings have occurred in 2026.
We are seeing unprecedented options activity right now.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US nonfarm labor productivity rose at a +3.5% annualized in Q3 2026, its largest increase...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US nonfarm labor productivity rose at a +3.5% annualized in Q3 2026, its largest increase since Q3 2025.
This also marks its 3rd consecutive quarterly improvement.
Nonfarm business output, which excludes the impact of government spending, surged at a +3.7% annualized rate, the strongest growth rate since Q3 2025.
Hourly compensation rose at a +2.9% annualized rate.
As productivity growth outpaced hourly compensation, unit labor costs, which measure labor costs per unit of output, declined -0.7% last quarter, the first quarterly decline since Q2 2025.
This largely a product of companies investing heavily in AI, software, and equipment to improve efficiency, increase output, and contain labor expenses.
AI is catalyzing a major US productivity surge.

item.title: @WOLF_Financial: GREG ABEL IS PUTTING BERKSHIRE'S CASH TO WORK In 2025, Warren Buffett's last year as CEO, Berkshire...
item.dc:creator: @WOLF_Financial
item.description:
GREG ABEL IS PUTTING BERKSHIRE'S CASH TO WORK
In 2025, Warren Buffett's last year as CEO, Berkshire was a net seller of stocks for the third straight year and didn't buy back a single share.
Under Greg Abel, it has turned net buyer.
In his first 9 months as CEO, Berkshire has:
- Bought back $14.4 billion of its own stock - Bought $11.2 billion more stock than it sold - Spent $16.2 billion on acquisitions, led by OxyChem and Taylor Morrison
That's about $42 billion of cash put to work.
And despite all that spending, Berkshire’s cash pile still sits at $377.4B, up from $373.3B at the end of 2025.

- Spent $16.2 billion on acquisitions, led by OxyChem and Taylor Morrison

item.dc:creator: @WOLF_Financial
item.description:
BERKSHIRE JUST MADE ITS BIGGEST BUYBACK EVER
Berkshire spent $9.6 billion buying back its own stock in Q3, topping its previous record of $9.3 billion from Q3 2020.
A year ago, it wasn't buying back a single share. Berkshire went six straight quarters without a buyback, from mid-2024 through the end of 2025.
September alone accounted for about $5.4 billion, at an average of $506.64 per Class B share.
Its favorite stock in Q3 was its own: Berkshire spent about four times as much on buybacks as on other companies' shares, buying $2.4 billion of stocks while selling $2.8 billion.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors surged +$12.1 billion i...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors surged +$12.1 billion in September, to a record $86.9 billion.
This marks the 2nd-largest monthly increase in history, following the record +$14.7 billion increase in July 2026.
Since the start of 2024, imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors have more than quadrupled.
YoY, these imports rose +151%, the largest YoY increase on record, compared with peak annual growth of just +34% during the 2000 Dot-Com Boom.
Based on September's figures, these imports are now running at an annualized rate above $1.0 trillion for the first time.
US demand for technology hardware is exploding.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global crude oil in transit is up to 1.28 billion barrels, an all-time high. This figure...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global crude oil in transit is up to 1.28 billion barrels, an all-time high.
This figure has surged +180 million barrels over the last several weeks.
This comes as Middle Eastern oil flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes, while more crude remains at sea for longer.
Ship-to-ship transfers are keeping oil aboard tankers for longer, while extended shipping routes are increasing transit times.
Meanwhile, global oil importers diversifying away from the Middle East are lengthening voyages, leaving more crude tied up aboard tankers.
As a result, more oil remains in transit rather than being readily available to refiners, tightening near-term supply despite recovering export flows.
Oil is flowing, but timely delivery is becoming the bottleneck.

item.title: @Hedgeye: 🇺🇸 Americans are borrowing to keep up: Consumer credit jumped $27.8 billion in September, the mos...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
🇺🇸 Americans are borrowing to keep up:
Consumer credit jumped $27.8 billion in September, the most since November 2022 and more than double the roughly $12 billion expected.
In the same month, real disposable income fell 0.3% and the personal saving rate slid to 3.8%, the lowest since October 2022.
This comes as inflation takes a bigger bite out of every paycheck.
With the PCE price index up 0.5% in a single month and CPI up 3.7% from a year ago, households leaned on credit just to keep real spending flat.
Credit card demand rose the most in four years in the Fed’s latest loan officer survey, and banks pointed to higher prices as the main reason.
That debt isn’t cheap. The average rate on cards charging interest is 22.36%, the highest in a year, and the Fed just raised rates for the first time since 2023.
The last time borrowing ran this hot and saving ran this thin was late 2022.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US job openings jumped +333,000 in September, to 7.52 million, the 3rd-highest reading si...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US job openings jumped +333,000 in September, to 7.52 million, the 3rd-highest reading since November 2024.
This marks the largest monthly increase since April and the 3rd-largestsince October 2024.
The surge was led by professional and business services, which added +106,000 openings.
State and local government, excluding education, followed, with an increase of +104,000.
As a result, the ratio of job openings to unemployed workers rose to 1.06, its highest since January 2025.
There are now 414,000 more available vacancies than unemployed workers, the 2nd-largest difference since January 2025.
US labor demand appears to be recovering.

item.description:
Retail demand for stocks is incredibly strong:
Retail investors purchased US equities in the 22 consecutive sessions ending November 3rd, the 3rd-longest streak since the memestock mania in 2021.
This also ranks as their 6th-longest purchasing streak since 2017.
Over this period, retail investors bought ~$33 billion in equities, their 5th-largest purchase since 2017.
This equals an average of ~$1.5 billion per trading session, and +40% above the trailing 12-month average.
Year-to-date, retail investors have purchased a record +$251 billion in equities, surpassing the previous full-year record of +$241 billion set in 2021 and marking a +134% increase from the same period last year.
Retail continues to buy the dip.

item.title: @wallstengine: $MSFT WINDS DOWN AI CLOUD DEAL WITH $ORCL Microsoft has reportedly declined to renew its 2023 agree...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$MSFT WINDS DOWN AI CLOUD DEAL WITH $ORCL
Microsoft has reportedly declined to renew its 2023 agreement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle and has been gradually shutting down that capacity in recent months, Bloomberg reports.
The deal was originally intended to power an AI-enhanced version of Bing.
However, the Oracle servers used older-generation Nvidia GPUs that no longer met Microsoft's computing specifications.
Oracle says demand for its AI infrastructure remains strong, including for older-generation GPUs.
item.content:encoded:
$MSFT WINDS DOWN AI CLOUD DEAL WITH $ORCL

Microsoft has reportedly declined to renew its 2023 agreement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle and has been gradually shutting down that capacity in recent months, Bloomberg reports.

The deal was originally intended to power an AI-enhanced version of Bing.

However, the Oracle servers used older-generation Nvidia GPUs that no longer met Microsoft's computing specifications.

Oracle says demand for its AI infrastructure remains strong, including for older-generation GPUs.

item.description:
Investors took record leverage into this week's decline:
US leveraged ETFs attracted +$9.5 billion in inflows in the week ending October 16th, their largest weekly intake on record in data going back to 2006.
This is more than double the previous weekly record inflow of +$4.5 billion, set in 2024.

At the same time, the 3x leveraged long Nasdaq 100 ETF, TQQQ, attracted +$1.3 billion.
Investors are highly levered amid the volatility.

item.title: @Hedgeye: The best part about risk managing Bear Markets? They bounce. The crowd sells the low end of the ran...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
The best part about risk managing Bear Markets? They bounce.
The crowd sells the low end of the range inside a Bearish TRADE and TREND. Then it buys the bounce toward the top end.
Backwards.
The process does the opposite. Cover some of your shorts near the LRR. Re-load into the bounce toward the TRR.
Same tape. Opposite playbook.

item.title: @wallstengine: TSMC WEIGHS MAKING 3D DRAM AT NVIDIA'S REQUEST $TSM has reportedly begun drawing up plans to manufa...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TSMC WEIGHS MAKING 3D DRAM AT NVIDIA'S REQUEST
$TSM has reportedly begun drawing up plans to manufacture advanced 3D DRAM chips as AI-driven memory shortages push chip designers to seek additional supply, per The Information.
Unlike conventional DRAM, 3D DRAM stacks memory cells vertically to increase density.
The move could put TSMC in direct competition with Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.
No production timeline has been set. TSMC is considering building new fabs or converting an existing facility, but says its focus remains on its core logic foundry business.

item.title: @wallstengine: $ASTS TO BUILD ITS OWN REUSABLE ROCKET AST SpaceMobile announced plans to develop Blacklift, a 20-t...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$ASTS TO BUILD ITS OWN REUSABLE ROCKET
AST SpaceMobile announced plans to develop Blacklift, a 20-ton reusable rocket designed to carry up to five BlueBird satellites per launch, with operations targeted for late 2028.
The company has signed a $1.3B+ agreement with Firefly Aerospace $FLY, which includes:
- Engines for the first three Blacklift rockets. - A perpetual license for AST to manufacture Firefly's Miranda and Vira engines at a new U.S. facility. - Engineering support over three years.
AST will pay approximately $800M upfront, consisting of $400M in cash and 10M–14M $ASTS shares, plus $250M for engines and $250M for engineering support.
Importantly, AST will continue using external launch providers, with existing agreements covering more than 100 BlueBird satellites for deployment in 2027–2028.
AST plans to unveil Blacklift on November 12 in New York City.
item.content:encoded:
$ASTS TO BUILD ITS OWN REUSABLE ROCKET

AST SpaceMobile announced plans to develop Blacklift, a 20-ton reusable rocket designed to carry up to five BlueBird satellites per launch, with operations targeted for late 2028.

The company has signed a $1.3B+ agreement with Firefly Aerospace $FLY, which includes:

- Engines for the first three Blacklift rockets.
- A perpetual license for AST to manufacture Firefly's Miranda and Vira engines at a new U.S. facility.
- Engineering support over three years.

AST will pay approximately $800M upfront, consisting of $400M in cash and 10M–14M $ASTS shares, plus $250M for engines and $250M for engineering support.

Importantly, AST will continue using external launch providers, with existing agreements covering more than 100 BlueBird satellites for deployment in 2027–2028.

AST plans to unveil Blacklift on November 12 in New York City.

$FLY has signed a 3-year agreement with AST SpaceMobile to supply engines for AST's new heavy-lift rocket.

Under the deal:

Firefly will deliver 36 engines, including 27 Miranda and 9 Vira engines, for AST's first three rockets.

AST will receive a license to manufacture the engines, along with engineering support. Firefly retains ownership of the engine IP.

AST will pay Firefly more than $1.3B in a combination of cash and ASTS shares, with the shares subject to lock-up periods.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US diesel inventories dropped -3.6 million barrels last week, to 99.3 million barrels, th...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US diesel inventories dropped -3.6 million barrels last week, to 99.3 million barrels, the lowest level since May 2003.
Since January 2026, distillate fuel oil inventories have declined -33.7 million barrels, or -25%.
Furthermore, the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -399,000 barrels last week, to 282.2 million barrels, its lowest since October 1982.
Since March, oil inventories in the SPR have dropped by -133.2 million barrels, or -32%.
Meanwhile, commercial crude oil stocks excluding the SPR declined -865,000 barrels last week, to 409.8 million barrels, their lowest reading since July 31st.
US fuel reserves are being depleted at a rapid pace.

item.title: @wallstengine: The future of robotics might involve a lot less real-world training. Think about it. Training physi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
The future of robotics might involve a lot less real-world training.
Think about it. Training physical robots through trial and error is expensive, slow and difficult to scale.
Moonlake just demonstrated it.
Starting with only 50 real-world demos, they ran reinforcement learning across 384 simulated environments, all at once.
And the improvements actually carried over to the physical robot. In one sorting test, it went from correctly sorting 6 out of 45 parts to 23. https://x.com/moonlake/status/2118405991662493737/video/1

item.title: @wallstengine: The IRS has increased the income thresholds for its 2027 tax brackets, as shown in the chart. Here'...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
The IRS has increased the income thresholds for its 2027 tax brackets, as shown in the chart.
Here's how much less you'd owe in federal income tax if your income stays the same as in 2026.
Single filers: $50K salary: $68 less $100K salary: $281 less $250K: $923 less
Married filing jointly: $100K combined income: $136 less $200K combined income: $561 less $500K combined income: $1,846 less
All seven tax rates remain unchanged. The savings come from wider income brackets and higher standard deductions.
Calculations assume the standard deduction, with no additional deductions or tax credits.
item.content:encoded:
The IRS has increased the income thresholds for its 2027 tax brackets, as shown in the chart.

Here's how much less you'd owe in federal income tax if your income stays the same as in 2026.

Single filers:
$50K salary: $68 less
$100K salary: $281 less
$250K: $923 less

Married filing jointly:
$100K combined income: $136 less
$200K combined income: $561 less
$500K combined income: $1,846 less

All seven tax rates remain unchanged. The savings come from wider income brackets and higher standard deductions.

Calculations assume the standard deduction, with no additional deductions or tax credits.

$IREN says it is implementing a network design change requested by Microsoft across its Horizon deployments.
Under its contract, delivery dates can be extended without delay credits for delays caused by such changes.

Discussions are still ongoing regarding delivery dates, fees, credits and cost reimbursements.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Anthropic has now disclosed a record $895 billion in future AI infrastructure spending commitments....
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Anthropic has now disclosed a record $895 billion in future AI infrastructure spending commitments.
This includes both purchase commitments and leases for computing power and related infrastructure.
$448 billion, or 50%, is expected to be incurred by the end of 2030, with ~$70 billion due over the next 12 months.
The biggest commitments are to Broadcom, $AVGO, at $161 billion, followed by Google at $121 billion, with up to $150 billion in additional estimated spending on Google's AI chips.
Anthropic has also committed up to $121 billion to SpaceX, $SPCX, and at least $110 billion to Amazon, $AMZN.
For perspective, among Big Tech companies, only Alphabet, $GOOGL, has larger commitments, at $1.06 trillion, while Meta, $META, follows with $866 billion.
The scale of Anthropic's spending obligations is unprecedented.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: On today's stock market crash: As an investor, on days like today, you have to ask yourself one que...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
On today's stock market crash:
As an investor, on days like today, you have to ask yourself one question: What fundamentally changed over the last 24 hours?
The shift in the fundamental backdrop cannot be attributed solely to the Midterm Election results; markets had already largely priced in the outcome.
So, what changed between yesterday and today? What is the fundamental reason for today's decline?
One of the most likely catalysts is growing concern about a potential "ban" on AI, or at the very least, severe regulation of the industry.
Over the last 24 hours, Democratic lawmakers have publicly called for restrictions on advanced AI development, including an outright "ban on artificial superintelligence."
Frankly, an outright ban will not happen.
Such a ban, if even possible to enforce, would effectively mean the US surrendering its position in the global AI race to China.
Does this mean AI is "over" or today's stock market crash marks "the end?" Absolutely not.
Rather, we believe we are witnessing a sudden shift in sentiment colliding with excessive levels of leverage, potentially triggering forced liquidations by several major institutional investors.
Therefore, today's downturn is more technical than fundamental. This is not to discount the concerns around regulation, they are legitimate. But price action right now does not look orderly or rational.
We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in human history.
Zoom out and remain calm.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Inflation has more than wiped out all US consumer wage gains since the 2020 Pandemic: US consumer p...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Inflation has more than wiped out all US consumer wage gains since the 2020 Pandemic:
US consumer prices have risen +31.3% since April 2020, to an all-time high in September.
Over the same period, average hourly earnings have increased just +25.9%.
This comes as CPI inflation has now been above the Fed’s 2% target for 67 consecutive months, the 3rd-longest streak over the last 100 years.
The only 2 longer streaks lasted 242 months, ending in 1986, and 128 months, ending in 1997.
Inflation continues to erode the spending power of Americans.

This also marks the strongest YoY growth since January 1974.
South Korea’s exports have now recorded 5 consecutive months with YoY growth of at least +60%.

item.content:encoded:
BREAKING: South Korea's exports surged +94% YoY in October, to $115 billion, the 2nd-highest reading on record.

This also marks the strongest YoY growth since January 1974.

South Korea’s exports have now recorded 5 consecutive months with YoY growth of at least +60%.

In the first 10 months of 2026, exports totaled a record $930 billion.

Semiconductors led last month's surge, rising +259% YoY, to a record $56 billion.

At the same time, computer sales spiked +497% amid strong demand for AI servers.

The AI boom has turned South Korea into an export powerhouse.

item.title: @wallstengine: Goldman Sachs $GS and Apollo $APO are approaching Wall Street investors to sell portions of SpaceX...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Goldman Sachs $GS and Apollo $APO are approaching Wall Street investors to sell portions of SpaceX $SPCX's roughly $40B AI chip financing deal.
The two firms have begun marketing the financing to potential buyers, with some investors being offered portions worth as much as $500M ahead of the formal syndication process, which is expected to begin soon.
The financing, announced in October, is the largest GPU financing arrangement on record.
Here's how the deal is structured:
An Apollo-backed entity will purchase approximately $47.3B worth of Nvidia GPUs and related equipment, primarily its next-generation Rubin chips.
The purchases will be financed through roughly $40B in debt, alongside a $7B lease prepayment from SpaceX.
SpaceX will then lease the chips for approximately five years, using a structure designed to keep the financing debt off its own balance sheet and protect its credit ratings.
The debt package includes an $8.3B senior-secured loan, alongside multiple bond tranches being marketed to institutional investors.
The Nvidia chips are expected to be delivered in the first half of 2027.
One interesting detail is that SpaceX's rental obligations remain unconditional.
The company must continue making payments even if the equipment is damaged or extraordinary events disrupt operations. SpaceX also isn't providing a guarantee covering the chips' residual value at the end of the lease.
Source: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
Goldman Sachs $GS and Apollo $APO are approaching Wall Street investors to sell portions of SpaceX $SPCX's roughly $40B AI chip financing deal.

The two firms have begun marketing the financing to potential buyers, with some investors being offered portions worth as much as $500M ahead of the formal syndication process, which is expected to begin soon.

The financing, announced in October, is the largest GPU financing arrangement on record.

Here's how the deal is structured:

An Apollo-backed entity will purchase approximately $47.3B worth of Nvidia GPUs and related equipment, primarily its next-generation Rubin chips.

The purchases will be financed through roughly $40B in debt, alongside a $7B lease prepayment from SpaceX.

SpaceX will then lease the chips for approximately five years, using a structure designed to keep the financing debt off its own balance sheet and protect its credit ratings.

The debt package includes an $8.3B senior-secured loan, alongside multiple bond tranches being marketed to institutional investors.

The Nvidia chips are expected to be delivered in the first half of 2027.

One interesting detail is that SpaceX's rental obligations remain unconditional.

The company must continue making payments even if the equipment is damaged or extraordinary events disrupt operations. SpaceX also isn't providing a guarantee covering the chips' residual value at the end of the lease.

Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The era of massive Big Tech stock buybacks is over. Combined buybacks by Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon,...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The era of massive Big Tech stock buybacks is over.
Combined buybacks by Alphabet, $GOOGL, Amazon, $AMZN, Microsoft, $MSFT, Meta, $META, and Oracle, $ORCL, fell to $4.4 billion in Q3 2026, the lowest since Q3 2017.
Share repurchases have dropped -90% since the ~$45.9 billion peak recorded in Q4 2021.
This also marks the 3rd consecutive quarter with buybacks below $5.0 billion.
This comes as Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle have not purchased their own stock in 2026.
By comparison, combined buybacks by these Big Tech companies stood at +$33.0 billion in Q1 2026.
AI spending is coming at the expense of Big Tech buybacks.

item.title: @Hedgeye: McCullough: This Hike Will Look Like A Policy Mistake 🔊 On the Free Edition of The Macro Show this...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
McCullough: This Hike Will Look Like A Policy Mistake
🔊
On the Free Edition of The Macro Show this morning, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough covered why the Fed is set up for a policy mistake.
Inflation reports lag the economy, and the next couple are still ticking up, which gives the Fed cover to raise rates in December.
As Keith put it, that hike “is going to look like a policy mistake,” because it lands just as the AI bubble and the credit tied to it start to crack.
Raising rates into a slowdown is how a wobble becomes a panic, and when that panic hits, the Fed does what it always does, cuts rates, which only makes it worse.
The tell is in the bond market.
Longer-term yields are already falling because they see growth and inflation slowing ahead.
Keith also flagged the timing, the last major cycle peaked in October 2007, the same month he was fired from Carlyle for being too bearish, right before the crash.
Watch the full episode of The Macro Show here: https://app.hedgeye.com/insights/189400-watch-for-free-the-macro-show-markets-midterms-the-road-to-quad?type=macro%2Cmarket-insights

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: This is highly unusual: The S&P 500 is trading more than 2 standard deviations below its 50-day mov...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
This is highly unusual:
The S&P 500 is trading more than 2 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, the first such occurrence since April.
Such a reading puts the S&P 500 in historically extreme oversold territory.
At the same time, only ~17% of the index’s stocks are now oversold, near its lowest proportion since July.
Meanwhile, ~47% of stocks are now overbought, the highest proportion since early February.
This figure has more than doubled since the start of October as many stocks have rallied beneath the surface.
The broader market looks far healthier than the S&P 500's recent performance suggests.

item.title: @Hedgeye: "These walls are funny. First you hate 'em. Then you get used to 'em. Enough time passes, you get s...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
"These walls are funny. First you hate 'em. Then you get used to 'em. Enough time passes, you get so you depend on 'em." - Red, The Shawshank Redemption
Same goes for bubbles.
First you hate getting squeezed by one. Then you start buying the damn dips in it. Enough time passes, you depend on it.
Then the walls close in.
That's how the Macro Tourist gets institutionalized. Every bubble. Every cycle.
Andy Dufresne didn't wait for the walls to close before he started digging. He had a plan years ahead of time.
Yours can be a lot simpler than a rock hammer and a poster. Know your MAX size before you buy. Know your TRADE and TREND lines. Know exactly what you do when both break.

item.title: @wallstengine: Oracle $ORCL has reportedly canceled a $7B AI chip leasing deal with Tencent following pressure fro...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Oracle $ORCL has reportedly canceled a $7B AI chip leasing deal with Tencent following pressure from the Trump administration, according to the FT.
The five-year agreement would have given Tencent access to as many as 100,000 advanced AI chips across Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia, making it Tencent's largest overseas chip leasing deal.
The arrangement would have allowed Tencent to use advanced computing hardware unavailable inside China because of U.S. and Chinese restrictions.
U.S. officials reportedly approached Oracle with concerns about the agreement. Meanwhile, senior Chinese officials visited Tencent and urged the company to support domestic chipmakers.
Although overseas AI chip leasing remains permitted under existing rules, the deal has now been canceled following pressure from both Washington and Beijing.
Oracle, Tencent, and the White House have not publicly commented on the reported cancellation.

item.title: @wallstengine: TEXAS TURNS BLUE IN A HISTORIC DOUBLE FLIP Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseats Gov. Greg Abbott, becomin...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TEXAS TURNS BLUE IN A HISTORIC DOUBLE FLIP
Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseats Gov. Greg Abbott, becoming Texas's first Democratic governor since Ann Richards was elected in 1990.
Democrat James Talarico also defeats Ken Paxton in the U.S. Senate race, marking the first Democratic Senate victory in Texas since 1988.
This ends Republicans' 32-year winning streak in Texas statewide elections.
The outcome could also have major implications for Texas's AI data center boom and ERCOT's power grid.
Hinojosa has called for a moratorium on new data center development, stricter power and water regulations, and an end to data center tax breaks.
Jefferies estimates that a Hinojosa victory could put 13.1 GW of announced Texas data center projects at immediate risk.
item.content:encoded:
TEXAS TURNS BLUE IN A HISTORIC DOUBLE FLIP

Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseats Gov. Greg Abbott, becoming Texas's first Democratic governor since Ann Richards was elected in 1990.

Democrat James Talarico also defeats Ken Paxton in the U.S. Senate race, marking the first Democratic Senate victory in Texas since 1988.

This ends Republicans' 32-year winning streak in Texas statewide elections.

The outcome could also have major implications for Texas's AI data center boom and ERCOT's power grid.

Hinojosa has called for a moratorium on new data center development, stricter power and water regulations, and an end to data center tax breaks.

Jefferies estimates that a Hinojosa victory could put 13.1 GW of announced Texas data center projects at immediate risk.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US federal debt surged +$422 billion in October, to a record $40.6 trillion. Since July 1...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US federal debt surged +$422 billion in October, to a record $40.6 trillion.
Since July 1st alone, US federal debt has soared +$1.2 trillion, averaging +$300 billion per month.
This is equivalent to an increase of ~$10 billion per day.
As a result, the US total public Debt-to-GDP ratio is up to 123%, the highest since the 2020 pandemic peak.
