item.title: @wallstengine: $ANET +18% JUST POSTED ITS FASTEST REVENUE GROWTH SINCE GOING PUBLIC IN 2014, UP 58.5% YOY. Arista...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$ANET +18%
JUST POSTED ITS FASTEST REVENUE GROWTH SINCE GOING PUBLIC IN 2014, UP 58.5% YOY.
Arista beat Wall Street expectations in Q3 and guided Q4 above estimates, while introducing a 2027 outlook well ahead of expectations.
Despite ramping investments in AI networking, liquid cooling, and high-speed switching, Arista delivered a 49.1% adjusted operating margin.
The company also raised its 2026 revenue guidance for the fourth time this year to $13.3B, representing 48% annual growth.
Looking ahead to 2027, management expects approximately $18.5B in revenue, or 38%-40% growth. That's well above the roughly $16.4B analysts were modeling before earnings.
AI networking is expected to drive much of that growth.
Arista expects its AI fabrics business to approximately double from at least $3.5B in 2026 to around $7B in 2027, accounting for nearly 38% of total company revenue next year.
Meanwhile, its campus networking business is projected to grow 60% to approximately $2B.
CEO Jayshree Ullal said Arista has now surpassed 100 Etherlink customers, compared with just four or five major AI customers when the company began its AI networking push a few years ago.
By the end of 2027, Arista expects more than 10 gigawatts of AI deployments across at least 10 different types of compute accelerators.
Another interesting development is the shift from centralized AI training toward distributed inference, where different parts of a workload, including prefill and token generation, run across separate systems.
That requires more networking capacity and more intelligent routing between GPUs, memory, and storage. Arista sees this as another growth opportunity beyond traditional AI data center networking.
The company is also expanding into scale-up Ethernet, which connects accelerators within and across racks, with customer trials expected in 2027 and production targeted for 2028.
item.content:encoded:
$ANET +18%

JUST POSTED ITS FASTEST REVENUE GROWTH SINCE GOING PUBLIC IN 2014, UP 58.5% YOY.

Arista beat Wall Street expectations in Q3 and guided Q4 above estimates, while introducing a 2027 outlook well ahead of expectations.

Despite ramping investments in AI networking, liquid cooling, and high-speed switching, Arista delivered a 49.1% adjusted operating margin.

The company also raised its 2026 revenue guidance for the fourth time this year to $13.3B, representing 48% annual growth.

Looking ahead to 2027, management expects approximately $18.5B in revenue, or 38%-40% growth. That's well above the roughly $16.4B analysts were modeling before earnings.

AI networking is expected to drive much of that growth.

Arista expects its AI fabrics business to approximately double from at least $3.5B in 2026 to around $7B in 2027, accounting for nearly 38% of total company revenue next year.

Meanwhile, its campus networking business is projected to grow 60% to approximately $2B.

CEO Jayshree Ullal said Arista has now surpassed 100 Etherlink customers, compared with just four or five major AI customers when the company began its AI networking push a few years ago.

By the end of 2027, Arista expects more than 10 gigawatts of AI deployments across at least 10 different types of compute accelerators.

Another interesting development is the shift from centralized AI training toward distributed inference, where different parts of a workload, including prefill and token generation, run across separate systems.

That requires more networking capacity and more intelligent routing between GPUs, memory, and storage. Arista sees this as another growth opportunity beyond traditional AI data center networking.

The company is also expanding into scale-up Ethernet, which connects accelerators within and across racks, with customer trials expected in 2027 and production targeted for 2028.

item.title: @wallstengine: $AMD RECORDED A $1.1B NON-CASH CHARGE TIED TO ITS OPENAI & META WARRANTS DEALS IN Q3 Buried in AMD'...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AMD RECORDED A $1.1B NON-CASH CHARGE TIED TO ITS OPENAI & META WARRANTS DEALS IN Q3
Buried in AMD's Q3 earnings reconciliation is a $1.097B change in the fair value of customer warrants, reducing GAAP EPS by $0.66.
Here's how it works.
Under its AI deals, OpenAI and Meta each received warrants to buy up to 160 million AMD shares at just $0.01 per share, or 320 million shares combined.
The warrants vest as customers meet GPU purchase commitments and AMD achieves specified stock-price milestones.
AMD must revalue these warrants every quarter based on its stock price and other assumptions. As their value increases, AMD records an accounting expense.
So the $1.1B charge wasn't cash paid to customers, but it was the largest single adjustment between AMD's $2.43B GAAP net income and $3.47B adjusted net income.
The other thing worth watching is the potential shareholder dilution if those warrants eventually vest and are exercised.
item.content:encoded:
$AMD RECORDED A $1.1B NON-CASH CHARGE TIED TO ITS OPENAI & META WARRANTS DEALS IN Q3

Buried in AMD's Q3 earnings reconciliation is a $1.097B change in the fair value of customer warrants, reducing GAAP EPS by $0.66.

Here's how it works.

Under its AI deals, OpenAI and Meta each received warrants to buy up to 160 million AMD shares at just $0.01 per share, or 320 million shares combined.

The warrants vest as customers meet GPU purchase commitments and AMD achieves specified stock-price milestones.

AMD must revalue these warrants every quarter based on its stock price and other assumptions. As their value increases, AMD records an accounting expense.

So the $1.1B charge wasn't cash paid to customers, but it was the largest single adjustment between AMD's $2.43B GAAP net income and $3.47B adjusted net income.

The other thing worth watching is the potential shareholder dilution if those warrants eventually vest and are exercised.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investors are rushing into Treasuries: The ratio of the Nasdaq 100 to the 20+ Year Treasury Bond ET...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investors are rushing into Treasuries:
The ratio of the Nasdaq 100 to the 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF, $TLT, is down to 342.5, its lowest since July 31st.
Since the all-time high recorded on October 7th, this ratio has fallen -15.4%.
Over this period, $TLT has risen +7.1%, while the Nasdaq 100 has fallen -10.2%.
This puts the ratio on track for its 5th consecutive weekly decline, its longest losing streak since the 2022 bear market.
Similar sharp drops in this metric were also recorded between February and April 2025 and during the 2020 pandemic.
Investors are buying bonds to protect against an AI selloff.

In 27 early-voting states that track voter registration by party, ~43% of early votes were by registered Democrats and ~32% by registered Republicans.
The first polls will close at 6 PM ET with the last polls closing at 1 AM ET.
Turn on our post notifications at @KobeissiLetter for real-time analysis as the day progresses.

item.description:
McCullough: A Volatility Regime Shift Is Underway
🔊
Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough covered what happens to markets when volatility shifts regimes on The Macro Show this morning.
The framework comes from the fractals that back-test across every Quad 4 Keith has called.
When an asset goes bearish TRADE and bearish TREND and enters a volatility regime shift, it moves from the investable bucket into the chop bucket, which is where the S&P 500 sits now.
The next step down is the worst bucket, and that’s where the Nasdaq already is, down -9%.
That’s a drawdown but not a crash, and Keith said he’d be shocked if the Nasdaq isn’t down more than 20% by the time the market reaches the throat of Quad 4, the really bad part, by Q2 of next year.
With Q4 nearly over, the market is starting to discount Q1. The warning for bulls is in the price action.
Futures bouncing, getting sold, then bouncing again doesn’t calm volatility, it amplifies the signal.
As Keith put it, “that’s fractal math. Those are the fractals. They know.”

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: It's officially election day. History says stocks are heading higher. In fact, the S&P 500 has clos...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
It's officially election day.
History says stocks are heading higher.
In fact, the S&P 500 has closed GREEN in the year following every US Midterm election since 1980.
As we noted in our analysis yesterday, we believe recent weakness in markets is largely a function of the uncertainty around Midterm elections.
However, when this uncertainty dissipates, markets react positively.
Since 1980, the S&P 500 has averaged a +14% gain in the 12 months following US Midterm elections.
Furthermore, even after divided-government outcomes, the index has averaged a +15% one-year gain, compared to +12% under single-party control.
Of course, the near-term picture will come with volatility and change.
But, if history is any guide, it's a great time to be bullish.
Turn on our post notifications at @KobeissiLetter for real-time analysis as this develops.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US semiconductor stocks have rarely been this volatile:
Over the last 5 mins S&P 500 Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment Index has recorded 11 trading sessions in which at least 50% of its components fell -5% or more, the 4th-highest reading on record.
By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, the index recorded 16 such sessions.
The only other periods with more volatility were 2000 and 2002, following the Dot-Com Bubble burst.
Furthermore, the S&P 500 Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment Index fell more than -5% on 12 trading days over the last 5 months.
The index is now down -32% from its June peak, trading at its lowest level since April.
Semiconductor stocks are experiencing historic volatility.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI infrastructure spending is driving a sharp increase in US bank lending: Commercial and Industria...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI infrastructure spending is driving a sharp increase in US bank lending:
Commercial and Industrial (C&I) loans at large US banks surged +11.4% YoY in October, to $1.6 trillion, the most since June 2020.
This also marked their largest YoY growth since February 2023.
In Q3, C&I loans at the 25 largest US banks grew almost +10.0% YoY, the strongest growth in 10 years excluding pandemic-related swings.
This represents a sharp reversal from an -8.0% YoY contraction in Q4 2025.
The surge has been driven by rising borrowing demand from Big Tech companies and data-center developers to fund AI infrastructure projects.
At the same time, regional lenders are providing credit to construction companies and other businesses benefiting from the investment boom.
The data-center buildout is increasingly being funded by debt.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, and Oracle, $ORCL, have n...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, and Oracle, $ORCL, have now disclosed a record $3.3 trillion in future spending commitments.
These are off-balance-sheet commitments covering data-center spending, future equipment purchases, leases, and other obligations.
$GOOGL accounts for the largest amount at $1.06 trillion, with its disclosed commitments surging nearly +700% over the last year.
$META follows at $866 billion, with nearly half tied to data-center leases that have not yet commenced and payment periods extending up to 30 years.
Meanwhile, Microsoft, $MSFT, has $593 billion in commitments, followed by Amazon, $AMZN, at $453 billion, and Oracle, $ORCL, at $322 billion.
The AI infrastructure buildout is creating an unprecedented pipeline of future financial obligations.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Leverage is skyrocketing in this market: US leveraged ETFs have attracted +$15 billion in inflows o...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Leverage is skyrocketing in this market:
US leveraged ETFs have attracted +$15 billion in inflows over the last month, their largest 1-month rolling inflow in at least 2 years.
This marks a sharp reversal from -$2 billion seen in early October.
By comparison, during the April 2025 market recovery, this figure peaked at +$12 billion.
The surge has been primarily led by retail investor demand for leveraged tech equity ETFs.
The 3x leveraged long Semiconductor ETF, $SOXL, alone attracted +$7.3 billion in October, its largest monthly inflow on record.
Retail investors are aggressively piling into leveraged equity ETFs.

item.description:
OPENAI HIRES FORMER U.S. ARMY SECRETARY: FT
Dan Driscoll will join OpenAI as senior counselor for national security modernization, helping the company expand AI adoption across U.S. and allied defense institutions.
An Iraq War veteran and close friend of Vice President JD Vance, Driscoll previously pushed to accelerate military technology adoption before resigning amid tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The appointment follows OpenAI's recent agreement to deploy its AI models in classified Pentagon environments after the military's negotiations with Anthropic broke down.
item.content:encoded:
OPENAI HIRES FORMER U.S. ARMY SECRETARY: FT

Dan Driscoll will join OpenAI as senior counselor for national security modernization, helping the company expand AI adoption across U.S. and allied defense institutions.

An Iraq War veteran and close friend of Vice President JD Vance, Driscoll previously pushed to accelerate military technology adoption before resigning amid tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

The appointment follows OpenAI's recent agreement to deploy its AI models in classified Pentagon environments after the military's negotiations with Anthropic broke down.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: What's happening now in the stock market is more than just a "correction in tech stocks." Sure, AI...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
What's happening now in the stock market is more than just a "correction in tech stocks."
Sure, AI CapEx concerns are legitimate and investors will always care about profitability.
But, there's more beneath the surface here.
The reality is that the market is pricing-in a major shift in the political landscape of the US.
Over the last 12 months, market expectations for a Democrat "sweep" of the US Midterm elections have tripled.
Over the last 45 days alone, these expectations are up +30 percentage points.
As it stands, markets themselves now see a near-80% chance of a Democrat "sweep" of the US Midterm elections.
President Trump has already vowed to become "Mr. Veto" if this in fact does happen.
This is post is not political, it's objective. A change in the political landscape always comes with uncertainty; markets hate uncertainty.
Objectively, the market is in the process of pricing-in two years of political gridlock.
Could this change? Of course. But markets price-in the most probable outcome, and the odds now overwhelmingly favor the aforementioned scenario.
Tomorrow sets the stage for the next two years.

item.title: @wallstengine: PALANTIR SHOWS FINE-TUNED NVIDIA 4B AI MODEL BEATING GPT-6 ASTRA & CLAUDE SONNET 5.5 AT A FRACTION...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
PALANTIR SHOWS FINE-TUNED NVIDIA 4B AI MODEL BEATING GPT-6 ASTRA & CLAUDE SONNET 5.5 AT A FRACTION OF THE COST
In its Q3 business update, $PLTR revealed that a fine-tuned $NVDA Nemotron 3 Nano model with just 4 billion parameters outperformed much larger frontier models on a real-world customer task.
The results, based on classifying requests for information for construction firm McCarthy:
• NVIDIA Nemotron 4B: ~75% accuracy at $0.10 per million tokens.
• Claude Sonnet 5.5: ~66% accuracy at $4 per million tokens.
• GPT-6 Astra: ~62% accuracy at $20 per million tokens.
Palantir says the fine-tuned models are expected to save McCarthy approximately 30,000 drafting hours annually.
Separately, NVIDIA itself is now training open AI models on its own supply chain data inside Palantir's Ontology, spanning millions of parts and thousands of suppliers.
Jensen Huang says the partnership combines NVIDIA's Nemotron models with Palantir's Ontology to:
“Reason, plan and orchestrate the journey from wafer to token.”

item.title: @wallstengine: BLOOM ENERGY $BE & CALIFORNIA RESOURCES SIGN DEAL TO EXPLORE 1 GW+ OF POWER GENERATION IN CALIFORNI...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
BLOOM ENERGY $BE & CALIFORNIA RESOURCES SIGN DEAL TO EXPLORE 1 GW+ OF POWER GENERATION IN CALIFORNIA
The companies signed a non-binding MOU to develop solid-oxide fuel cell projects paired with carbon capture and storage.
Bloom would supply its fuel cell technology, while CRC's Carbon TerraVault would provide CO2 transportation and permanent storage.
The projects, being considered in Central and Northern California, could serve data centers, utilities and industrial customers.
The companies estimate up to 3 million metric tons of CO2 annually could be available for capture and storage.
Development remains subject to final agreements, investment decisions and regulatory approvals.

Major institutional investors are reportedly urging Anthropic to pursue a more conservative IPO valuation of $1.5T to $1.6T, well below the roughly $2T valuation discussed in recent months.
Some investors reportedly favor a lower starting valuation to leave room for a strong first-day trading gain, with expectations that Anthropic could potentially reach a $2T valuation after its market debut.

Anthropic is expected to begin its IPO roadshow as soon as next week, with its Nasdaq debut targeted for the week before Thanksgiving.

item.title: @HedgeyeENERGY: Introducing the Hedgeye Oil Model. We built a fair-value model for WTI based on global oil inventor...
item.dc:creator: @HedgeyeENERGY
item.description:
Introducing the Hedgeye Oil Model.
We built a fair-value model for WTI based on global oil inventories. Since 2011, it explains about 80% of WTI's price moves.
What it says today:
- WTI fair value is about $91 a barrel, with a ±$10 band. - WTI is $96 after today's 8% drop on Iran talks. That's inside the band. - The war premium peaked at $22 over fair value in March to May. - WTI then traded $2 to $5 below fair value in June to August as the market looked through the disruption. - The premium came back this fall, at about $7 in September and $11 in October. - For fair value to reach $105, OECD inventories need to draw about another 100 million barrels. At this year's pace, that's four to six months away. - On EIA's current estimates, fair value holds near $90 through year-end. If inventories rebuild in 2027 as EIA expects, fair value falls into the $60s by mid-2027.
Bottom line: on inventories, oil is fairly priced. The upside case needs more draws, not more headlines.
We'll update the model regularly as new inventory data comes in.
item.content:encoded:
Introducing the Hedgeye Oil Model.

We built a fair-value model for WTI based on global oil inventories. Since 2011, it explains about 80% of WTI's price moves.

What it says today:

- WTI fair value is about $91 a barrel, with a ±$10 band.
- WTI is $96 after today's 8% drop on Iran talks. That's inside the band.
- The war premium peaked at $22 over fair value in March to May.
- WTI then traded $2 to $5 below fair value in June to August as the market looked through the disruption.
- The premium came back this fall, at about $7 in September and $11 in October.
- For fair value to reach $105, OECD inventories need to draw about another 100 million barrels. At this year's pace, that's four to six months away.
- On EIA's current estimates, fair value holds near $90 through year-end. If inventories rebuild in 2027 as EIA expects, fair value falls into the $60s by mid-2027.

Bottom line: on inventories, oil is fairly priced. The upside case needs more draws, not more headlines.

We'll update the model regularly as new inventory data comes in.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US equity funds recorded -$6.7 billion in outflows in the week ending October 28th, their largest weekly withdrawal since mid-September.
This follows +$5.1 billion and +$13.0 billion in inflows over the previous two weeks.
Meanwhile, global equity funds attracted +$10.2 billion in the week ending October 28th, marking their 6th consecutive weekly intake.
However, this was down from +$25.1 billion and +$19.8 billion in the preceding two weeks.
Asian equity funds led last week's inflows, attracting +$9.9 billion, compared with +$11.6 billion the previous week.
At the same time, European equity funds attracted +$4.5 billion.
Global investors are rotating out of US equities into other regions.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Markets are heading into their strongest seasonal period of the year: Since 1980, the S&P 500 has r...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Markets are heading into their strongest seasonal period of the year:
Since 1980, the S&P 500 has rallied +2.1% on average in November, making it the strongest month of the year.
Over this period, positive returns occurred 74% of the time, the best hit rate of any month.
Furthermore, the S&P 500 has gained +1.6% on average in November since 1964, with positive returns occurring 69% of the time.
The highest November return during this period was +10.8%, recorded in 2020.
During midterm years, November has averaged +2.7% since 1950, with a 78.9% win rate.
History points to a strong month ahead.

Keith added $BNDD, a disinflation ETF, to position for falling long-term bond yields.

item.description:
Tokenization is the biggest bull market in crypto.
The total circulating supply of onchain tokenized equities just hit another record high, at $3.8 billion.
This metric has now reached a new record high for 10 consecutive weeks, up +590% year-to-date.
It has become increasingly clear that financial markets are moving toward tokenizing everything.
Investors are demanding 24/7 markets, and tokenized assets are increasingly fulfilling that demand.
Amid the shift, Jupiter, the largest onchain platform on Solana, reported that 70% of tokenized asset trading now occurs outside traditional market hours.
Amid this surge in demand, the NYSE is developing infrastructure for tokenized equities and perpetual futures.
The future of financial markets is onchain.

item.title: @wallstengine: HUME LAUNCHES AN API THAT ANALYZES HOW PEOPLE SOUND A confident “sure” and a hesitant “…sure” can l...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
HUME LAUNCHES AN API THAT ANALYZES HOW PEOPLE SOUND
A confident “sure” and a hesitant “…sure” can look identical in a transcript. Hume’s Decision API analyzes the recording itself, including tone, pauses and interruptions.
Developers provide: • An audio clip • A question, such as “Does the caller sound unsure?” • Possible answers
The API returns a probability for each answer, trained to reflect how human listeners would respond.
Those scores could help voice-agent teams decide when to ask for clarification, review a call or assess how naturally their agent responds.
https://x.com/hume_ai/status/2117285608745820372/video/1
item.content:encoded:
HUME LAUNCHES AN API THAT ANALYZES HOW PEOPLE SOUND

A confident “sure” and a hesitant “…sure” can look identical in a transcript. Hume’s Decision API analyzes the recording itself, including tone, pauses and interruptions.

Developers provide:
• An audio clip
• A question, such as “Does the caller sound unsure?”
• Possible answers

The API returns a probability for each answer, trained to reflect how human listeners would respond.

Those scores could help voice-agent teams decide when to ask for clarification, review a call or assess how naturally their agent responds.

item.title: @wallstengine: OpenAI announced its new Grid Protectors program, designed to reduce electricity use at future AI d...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OpenAI announced its new Grid Protectors program, designed to reduce electricity use at future AI data centers when local power grids are strained.
Its planned Georgia campus is expected to require 3.2GW of power, but could reduce demand by up to 1GW during peak periods, equivalent to the average electricity use of roughly 700,000 homes.
The campus is still in development.
OpenAI says it will cover the full electricity and grid infrastructure costs.

The firm increased its estimates by: • 2026: +9% • 2027: +7% • 2028: +17%

However, new hyperscaler backlog additions slowed to $128B from $237B in Q2, even as total backlog continued growing 142% YoY.

item.title: @wallstengine: $MRVL TO ACQUIRE $LITE IN $115B ALL-STOCK DEAL Marvell has agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-sto...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$MRVL TO ACQUIRE $LITE IN $115B ALL-STOCK DEAL
Marvell has agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $115B in enterprise value, combining two major suppliers of AI infrastructure and optical networking technology.
Under the agreement:
• Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each LITE share, implying roughly $1,132 per share.
• The offer represents a 23.9% premium to unaffected closing prices on October 28.
• Marvell shareholders will own approximately 67% of the combined company, with Lumentum shareholders holding 33%.
The deal brings together Marvell's custom AI chips, networking switches and interconnect technology with Lumentum's lasers, optical transceivers and optical circuit switching capabilities.
The bigger opportunity is the growing shift from copper to optical connectivity as AI data centers require faster data transfer, greater bandwidth and improved power efficiency.
Marvell says the combination could expand its addressable market to $550B, allowing it to offer more integrated connectivity solutions across AI data centers and within advanced chip packages.
The companies also expect:
• More than $1B in annual run-rate cost synergies.
• Improved long-term revenue growth and profit margins.
• Accretion to Marvell's adjusted EPS in the first year after closing.
Matt Murphy will remain CEO of the combined company, with the transaction expected to close in H1 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
Separately, Marvell reaffirmed the midpoint of its fiscal Q3 revenue guidance while narrowing the expected range to ±2% from ±5%.
item.content:encoded:
$MRVL TO ACQUIRE $LITE IN $115B ALL-STOCK DEAL

Marvell has agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $115B in enterprise value, combining two major suppliers of AI infrastructure and optical networking technology.

Under the agreement:

• Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each LITE share, implying roughly $1,132 per share.

• The offer represents a 23.9% premium to unaffected closing prices on October 28.

• Marvell shareholders will own approximately 67% of the combined company, with Lumentum shareholders holding 33%.

The deal brings together Marvell's custom AI chips, networking switches and interconnect technology with Lumentum's lasers, optical transceivers and optical circuit switching capabilities.

The bigger opportunity is the growing shift from copper to optical connectivity as AI data centers require faster data transfer, greater bandwidth and improved power efficiency.

Marvell says the combination could expand its addressable market to $550B, allowing it to offer more integrated connectivity solutions across AI data centers and within advanced chip packages.

The companies also expect:

• More than $1B in annual run-rate cost synergies.

• Improved long-term revenue growth and profit margins.

• Accretion to Marvell's adjusted EPS in the first year after closing.

Matt Murphy will remain CEO of the combined company, with the transaction expected to close in H1 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

Separately, Marvell reaffirmed the midpoint of its fiscal Q3 revenue guidance while narrowing the expected range to ±2% from ±5%.
